subtitle: How a cautious minister held a storm-tossed throne for a child Peshwa

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot in dim court
panels.action: Nana Fadnavis stands in the shadowed hall of Shaniwar Wada, scrolls in hand, a child’s throne looming behind him as dusky Pune skies glow faintly beyond carved arches.

dialogue.text: In the age of gunpowder and Company gold, Nana Fadnavis guarded a child’s throne and tried to bind a restless Maratha confederacy with paper, patience and fear.

i18n.hi: बारूद और कंपनी की सोने की दुनिया में, नाना फड़नवीस ने बाल तख़्त की रखवाली की और बिखरे मराठों को काग़ज़, सब्र और डर से बाँधने की जुगत की।

panels.shot: wide interior of Shaniwar Wada with deep perspective
panels.action: Inside Shaniwar Wada’s audience hall, courtiers whisper in tense clusters while Nana Fadnavis stands apart near a pillar, face grave, as a palanquin bearing the slain Narayanrao is carried away in the background.

dialogue.text: In 1773, Shaniwar Wada shook. Peshwa Narayanrao lay dead, his blood-feud leaving no clear heir, only fear in the courtyards of Pune.

i18n.hi: १७७३ में शनिवार वाड़ा काँप उठा। पेशवा नारायणराव मारे गए, खून की दुश्मनी ने वारिस नहीं छोड़ा, बस पूना के आँगनों में डर भर दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Nana at a low lamp-lit desk
panels.action: By the light of a single oil lamp, Nana Fadnavis bends over a spread of letters and roznama pages, his pen poised, while shadowy hints of rival sardars loom beyond the doorway.

dialogue.text: Nana, son of a Deshastha family risen through service, was already keeper of accounts and letters. The Daftar was his battlefield, ink his chosen sword.

i18n.hi: सेवा से उठी देशस्थ खानदान का बेटा नाना, पहले ही हिसाब-किताब और खतों का रखवाला था। दफ्तार ही उसका मैदान था, स्याही उसकी तलवार।

panels.shot: council-table wide shot with figures half in shadow
panels.action: Around a long wooden table in a Pune manor, twelve Maratha nobles and ministers sit in heated discussion; Nana Fadnavis, calm yet firm, rests his hand on a scroll bearing an infant’s seal.

dialogue.text: Out of the crisis rose the Barabhai, the ‘twelve brothers’. Old houses of the Confederacy shared power, agreeing that the infant Madhavrao II would sit as Peshwa in name.

i18n.hi: संकट से उभरे बाराभाई, यानी ‘बारह भाई’। संघ के पुराने घराने जुटे, तय हुआ कि नन्हा माधवराव द्वितीय नाम भर का पेशवा बनेगा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nana beside a cradle-throne
panels.action: In the Diwan’s chamber, a small child in rich cloth sits on a raised, throne-like seat; Nana stands nearby with a protective, watchful gaze, courtiers bowing at a distance.

dialogue.text: A child was placed on the gaddi. Behind him, elders guarded their own claims. Nana, one among them, took the task of shielding the boy and the fragile prestige of Pune.

i18n.hi: एक बच्चा गद्दी पर बैठा दिया गया। पीछे बुज़ुर्ग अपनी-अपनी दावेदारी साधे रहे। नाना, उन्हीं में एक, ने बालक और पूना की नाज़ुक इज़्ज़त ढालने का भार लिया।

panels.shot: overhead view of Deccan map and scattered letters
panels.action: A detailed Deccan map lies spread on a floor mat, weighted by inkpots and seals, while Nana arranges piles of letters marked Poona, Nagpur, Gwalior and Seringapatam.

dialogue.text: Beyond Pune, the Confederacy stretched in long arcs: Scindia in the north, Bhonsles in Nagpur, Gaekwads in Baroda, Holkars in Malwa, and new sultans and Europeans watching from every horizon.

i18n.hi: पूना से बाहर, संघ दूर-दूर तक फैला था: उत्तर में शिंदे, नागपुर में भोंसले, बड़ौदा में गायकवाड़, मालवा में होलकर, और चारों ओर नए सुल्तान और फिरंगी ताकते नज़र गड़ाए।

panels.shot: medium shot at balcony overlooking Pune street
panels.action: From a carved balcony, Nana Fadnavis looks down at a busy Pune street where sepoys drill and traders lead bullock carts, a distant English factory flag seen above tiled roofs.

dialogue.text: To the west, the English Company crept inland with counting-houses and forts. They spoke as traders, but moved like rulers, measuring every fissure in Maratha politics.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम से अँग्रेज़ कंपनी गिनती-घरों और क़िलों के सहारे अंदर घुस रही थी। ज़ुबान से सौदागर, चाल से बादशाह, मराठा राज की हर दरार नापती हुई।

panels.shot: tense council close-wide inside Shaniwar Wada
panels.action: In a crowded council hall, Nana gestures toward a parchment as one fiery sardar slams his fist on the floor; others lean forward, half eager, half anxious.

dialogue.text: When disputes tore the Barabhai, some sought English help. Nana feared that once foreign troops entered Deccan quarrels, they would never leave.

i18n.hi: जब बाराभाई में फूट पड़ी, कुछ ने अँग्रेज़ी मदद माँगी। नाना को डर था, एक बार फिरंगी फौजें दक्खन के झगड़ों में उतरीं, तो फिर लौटेंगी नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Maratha camp outside Wadgaon hills
panels.action: On a rugged hillside near Wadgaon, Maratha tents and artillery ring a valley as British-red-coated troops stand surrounded, muskets lowered, under a hazy winter sky.

dialogue.text: War came in 1779. At Wadgaon, British forces were outmaneuvered in the ghats. The Treaty that followed forced them to restore their gains and humbled their Pune agents.

i18n.hi: १७७९ में जंग छिड़ी। वडगाँव के घाटों में अंग्रेज़ फौज मात खा गई। जो संधि हुई, उसने उनकी फ़तहें छुड़वाईं और पूना में बैठे उनके सरदारों का घमंड तोड़ा।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Nana negotiating with a British officer
panels.action: In a stately chamber, Nana sits cross-legged opposite a rigid British officer with powdered hair; between them lies a draft treaty bearing both Devanagari and English scripts.

dialogue.text: Yet victory brought choice. Some Marathas wanted harsher terms. Nana and his colleagues weighed gains against future storms from Bombay and Calcutta.

i18n.hi: पर जीत के साथ दुविधा आई। कुछ मराठे और सख्ती चाहते थे। नाना और उसके साथी ने फ़ायदे तौले, बंबई और कलकत्ता से उठने वाले भावी तूफ़ानों के ख़िलाफ़।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Nana’s thoughtful profile
panels.action: Close on Nana’s face as he studies the treaty, his eyes tired but steady, fingers lightly resting on a wax seal.

dialogue.speaker: nana_fadnavis
dialogue.text: Steel wins a field, but words decide how long we keep it.

i18n.hi: फौलाद मैदान जिताता है, पर ज़मीन कितने दिन रहेगी, यह लफ़्ज़ तय करते हैं।

panels.shot: wide diplomatic durbar with multiple envoys
panels.action: A grand durbar scene with Nana seated modestly to one side of the child Peshwa; in front stand envoys in varied dress, Maratha sardars on one side, a British representative and Persianate nobles on the other.

dialogue.text: The First Anglo-Maratha War dragged on. Across years, diplomacy stretched as long as campaigns. Each letter weighed alliance with Scindia, Bhonsle, even Mysore, against the Company’s hunger.

i18n.hi: पहला अँग्रेज़–मराठा युद्ध लंबा घिसटा। बरसों तक कूटनीति ने ही जंग जितनी दूरी तय की। हर खत में शिंदे, भोंसले, यहाँ तक कि मैसूर से यारी तौली गई, कंपनी की भूख के मुक़ाबले।

panels.shot: map-table shot focused on Salbai region
panels.action: Hands from different sides reach toward a map where the name Salbai is marked; Nana’s hand remains slightly withdrawn, as if measuring every concession.

dialogue.text: In 1782, the Treaty of Salbai was sealed. It confirmed Raghunathrao’s claims set aside, fixed frontiers, and brought a wary peace between the Peshwa’s court and the English Company.

i18n.hi: १७८२ में सालबाई की संधि पक्की हुई। रघुनाथराव के दावे हटाए गए, सरहदें ठहरीं, और पेशवा दरबार और अँग्रेज़ कंपनी के बीच एक सतर्क सुलह बनी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nana in correspondence with Scindia’s envoy
panels.action: Nana sits with an envoy bearing Scindia’s insignia, as a servant holds a tray of sealed letters bound for the north.

dialogue.text: To the north, Mahadji Scindia carved power around Delhi, placing puppet emperors and minting his own strength. Nana’s letters to him show alliance, rivalry and endless bargaining over prestige and revenue.

i18n.hi: उत्तर में महादजी शिंदे ने दिल्ली के इर्द-गिर्द ताकत गढ़ी, बादशाह बिठाए, अपनी मुहर चलवाई। नाना के खत उसमें दोस्ती भी दिखाते हैं, टक्कर भी, और इज़्ज़त व माली हक़ पर न खत्म होने वाली सौदेबाज़ी भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of council arguing about Mysore
panels.action: In another council, Nana listens as a Maratha sardar gestures angrily toward a map showing Mysore; a stylized tiger banner of Tipu Sultan is visible on the map.

dialogue.text: In the south, Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan challenged both Maratha and English claims. Some in Pune wanted firmer war, others trade. Nana’s caution sometimes meant lost chances and new resentments.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण में हैदर अली और टीपू सुल्तान ने मराठा और अँग्रेज़, दोनों के दावे ललकारे। पूना में कुछ लोग सख़्त जंग चाहते थे, कुछ सौदा। नाना की एहतियात ने कई मौके गँवाए, कई नए मलाल भी बोए।

panels.shot: dim corridor shot of Nana passing restless soldiers
panels.action: Nana walks down a stone corridor of Shaniwar Wada as armed retainers watch, some respectful, some cold-eyed, whispering among themselves.

dialogue.text: Colonial chroniclers later called him ‘Machiavellian’. His own records show something slower: a minister balancing factions, sometimes delaying decisions, sometimes letting chances rot rather than risk collapse.

i18n.hi: फिरंगी इतिहासकारों ने बाद में उसे ‘मैकियावेलियन’ कहा। उसके अपने काग़ज़ दिखाते हैं कुछ और: एक दीर्घ-साँस मंत्री, जो गुटों को साधता रहा, कभी फ़ैसले टालता, कभी जोखिम उठाने से बेहतर मौके सड़ने देता।

panels.shot: quiet interior with Nana teaching the young Peshwa
panels.action: In a calmer moment, Nana sits on a rug with the adolescent Madhavrao II, pointing to a ledger as the young Peshwa listens with mixed trust and impatience.

dialogue.text: He tried to school his Peshwa in ledgers and limits, not only battles. But a throne bound by elders is a throne chafing to be free.

i18n.hi: वह अपने पेशवा को सिर्फ़ जंग नहीं, हिसाब और हद सिखाना चाहता था। पर बुज़ुर्गों की रस्सियों से बँधा तख़्त, आज़ाद होने को हमेशा छटपटाता है।

panels.shot: somber court with news of Madhavrao II’s death
panels.action: Courtiers stand in mourning in the hall as word of Madhavrao II’s death spreads; Nana sits heavily, shoulders stooped, while a veiled figure is led away.

dialogue.text: When Madhavrao II died in 1795, whispers of poison and despair filled Pune. The Barabhai’s long guardianship ended in grief, not in the stable kingship they had hoped for.

i18n.hi: १७९५ में माधवराव द्वितीय की मौत पर ज़हर और मायूसी की फुसफुसाहटों ने पूना घेर लिया। बाराभाई की लंबी सरपरस्ती का अंत शोक में हुआ, उस ठोस राज में नहीं, जिसकी वे उम्मीद करते थे।

panels.shot: late-life close-up with piles of ageing documents
panels.action: An older Nana Fadnavis sits surrounded by tall stacks of worn papers, his fingers resting on a sealed bundle marked with his personal sign, a faint cough tightening his features.

dialogue.text: By the late 1790s, new strongmen like Daulat Rao Scindia and the English governors eyed Pune. Nana’s influence waned, his body slowing as the tempo of conquest quickened.

i18n.hi: १७९० के आख़िर तक दौलत राव शिंदे जैसे नए ताकतवर और अँग्रेज़ गवर्नर, दोनों की नज़र पूना पर थी। नाना का असर ढलने लगा, उसका शरीर धीमा पड़ गया, जबकि फ़तहों की रफ़्तार तेज़ हो गई।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Shaniwar Wada as storm clouds gather
panels.action: Shaniwar Wada rises against a darkening sky, lightning hinting at distant storm clouds, as the silhouette of Nana Fadnavis is seen small in an upper balcony arch.

dialogue.text: Nana died in 1800, just before the Second Anglo-Maratha War. Within a few years, British troops would march where his letters once ruled, and the Peshwa’s power would unravel.

i18n.hi: नाना १८०० में मरा, ठीक दूसरे अँग्रेज़–मराठा युद्ध से पहले। कुछ ही बरसों में वहीं अँग्रेज़ फौजें चलेंगी, जहाँ कभी उसके खत हुक्म चलाते थे, और पेशवा की ताकत उधड़ जाएगी।

panels.shot: final reflective close-up of a sealed Daftar bundle
panels.action: A close view of an old Daftar bundle tied with cotton string, Nana’s seal pressed into the wax, resting on a wooden desk lit by soft dawn light over Pune.

dialogue.text: His papers, surviving in the Peshwa Daftar, show no lone mastermind, but a careful minister who, with others, held a divided confederacy together for a generation by diplomacy more than by sword.

i18n.hi: पेशवा दफ्तार में बची उसकी फाइलें किसी अकेले दानिशवर की नहीं, एक सतर्क मंत्री की झलक देती हैं, जिसने औरों के साथ मिलकर, तलवार से ज़्यादा सियासत के बल पर, बँटे हुए संघ को एक पीढ़ी तक जोड़े रखा।

title_i18n.en: Nana Fadnavis and the Twelve Pillars

subtitle_i18n.en: How a cautious minister held a storm-tossed throne for a child Peshwa
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक समझदार मंत्री ने कैसे तूफ़ानी तख़्त को बाल पेशवा के लिए संभाला
